COMPONENT_GRAPH.mutation_path: Terraform desired intent -> resource model -> deterministic Ansible task/playbook generation -> structured ansible-playbook runner -> local Linux mutation.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.observation_path: Read/refresh bypasses mutation and uses native Linux observers -> canonical observed model -> Terraform Core state.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.provider_runtime: Terraform provider registration, configuration and preflight establish the local inventory/runtime context.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.resource_layer: file, directory, copy, template, line, block, symlink, user, group and cron use the same lifecycle/runner/observer infrastructure with family-specific ownership semantics.
COMPONENT_GRAPH.shared_lifecycle: Stable identity, transition/state-publication rules and canonical normalization are shared across all resources.

ENTRYPOINTS: provider configuration and supplied local inventory
Create/Read/Update/Delete callbacks for each of ten managed resources
structured ansible-playbook subprocess runner for mutation only
native Linux observation helpers for Read/refresh
PRODUCTION_CHARACTERISTICS: real Go Terraform Plugin Framework provider/runtime
idempotency and representation normalization across repeated plan/apply/refresh cycles
outputs.SCALE_FIT: PASS: large_system_strict; the coherent ten-resource provider spans multiple production-like components and cross-cutting lifecycle invariants rather than padded independent CRUD handlers.

STATE_MODEL.failure: nonzero exit, timeout or cancellation retains the last successfully applied state; failed delete remains managed and retryable
STATE_MODEL.publication: publish new applied state only after successful mutation
STATE_MODEL.refresh: native observation reflects drift and removes state when object is missing or wrong kind
STATE_MODEL.runtime_truth: external Linux objects and native observations
